text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000122's 99215 rate runs well above what its patient complexity predicts, and the excess shows up in every complexity band, but too few charts came back to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern is consistent with upcoding: 99215 share is elevated relative to all providers at every condition count, including patients with zero or one chronic conditions. The low-complexity sample includes 99215 claims for follow-up (Z09), UTI (N39.0) and low back pain (M54.50) visits, such as C0071916, C0072148 and C0072253, which would not usually call for high-complexity decision-making. Against that, the documentation is too thin to judge. Only 3 documented 99215 claims exist, and two low-complexity ones (C0071998, C0072309) were documented at high MDM with 45 to 52 minutes, so a single unsupported claim (C0072484) cannot set a rate. The 2 data-reviewed notes without a lab or test line are weak evidence of note inflation, not proof. A reviewer should first request a larger targeted sample of charts for the 0-1 condition 99215 claims, then check whether those notes show genuine high-complexity decision-making or templated or cloned text."}
